column7: Large-format collaboration combining an analog preamp/gain system with motorized sliders, preset recall and MIDI control. 2020 coverage identifies a broad overdrive range plus Fuzz Face-style fuzz capability.
column10: Preserve Automatone Preamp MKII as a distinct collaboration/product identity. The motorized controls, preset system and analog-audio/digital-control split are strong external markers.

column7: Compact second version of the Sunn O))) Life Pedal. EQD documents V2 as the same core circuit as the 2019 limited run, with expression control over octave blend and Flexi-Switch relay bypass, limited to 2,500 units worldwide.
column10: A critical generation rule: V2 is documented as the same core circuit with changed enclosure/control features, so it must not be treated automatically as a circuit redesign. Preserve V1 and V2 separately.

column7: Collaboration between Chase Bliss and ZVEX based on the Fuzz Factory concept, expanded with MIDI, expression and preset-oriented digital control. Limited production created a distinct modern specimen class.
column10: Preserve ZVEX Fuzz Factory lineage and Chase Bliss manufacturing/control identity separately. MIDI, preset behavior and collaboration status are core identification clues.

column7: Germanium fuzz device documented in 2020 annual coverage as a distinct Demedash fuzz product, with extensive control interaction and a strongly vintage-oriented germanium character.
column10: Keep Spidola distinct from other Demedash devices and preserve its 2020 product identity even where later availability changes.

column7: Analog fuzz with footswitchable octave section and a DIVIDE control blending one and two octaves down. Two-band EQ and interactive fuzz controls create a distinct heavy octave-fuzz identity; hand built in the UK.
column10: The footswitchable octave, -1/-2 octave blending, DIVIDE control and two-band EQ are strong external markers. Preserve Honey Badger separately from Redbeard's later Hairy Squid fuzz.

column7: Fourth-generation Fuzz God combining fuzz, Octavia and switchable parasitic oscillation. Builder documentation specifies two NOS BC109 transistors, Sputter bias control, Wrath oscillation, internal DIP configuration and three true-bypass footswitches; handmade in New Zealand.
column10: The IV generation is explicit and should remain separate from earlier Fuzz God versions. Three-mode structure, three footswitches, Sputter/Wrath controls and BC109 implementation are high-value identifiers.

column7: Third iteration of the Sputnik all-germanium fuzz family using NOS Soviet germanium transistors and diode, incorporating features from previous versions while adding its own voice and functionality.
column10: Treat Sputnik III as a genuine generation because the builder explicitly calls it the third iteration. Preserve earlier Sputnik and Sputnik II separately.

column7: Boutique ODR-style overdrive product documented in 2020 as a custom interpretation of the Nashville overdrive family, with a distinct Nordland product identity and component/voicing choices.
column10: Preserve the ODR family as lineage rather than identity. ODR-C is a Nordland product with its own enclosure and production history.

column7: Dual-channel extended-range overdrive based on Wampler's Pantheon Blues Breaker-derived platform, adding independent controls and stacking functionality. 2020 annual coverage places the Deluxe among notable dual overdrives.
column10: Preserve Pantheon Deluxe separately from the single Pantheon. The dual-channel enclosure and independent stacking controls form a separate production identity.
